model: Deal-weighted scheme valuation: deal-completes (PV of cash consideration) vs deal-breaks (owner-FCF component DCF, engine route)

equity_bridge.item: Non-controlling interests (FY26 guided NCI profit GBP20-21m x ~15x)
equity_bridge.note: H1 FY2026 outlook; FY2025 AR note 20 NCI equity GBP44.6m, NCI dividends GBP16.1m

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_5yr_cagr (4.6%) cross-checked against FY2026 guidance of mid-single-digit LFL growth and H1 FY2026 actual +5.9% reported / +6.1% constant currency
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-5.5% 3yr, +2.1% 5yr) diverges >30% from revenue/EPS because the GBP350m FY2025 buyback and GBP252m dividends shrank book equity; book value is not the growth anchor for a 21% ROIC asset-light business. Owner-FCF CAGR is negative (-5.6% 5yr) against +4.6% revenue: FY2020 was inflated by COVID working-capital inflows and FY2025 depressed by a GBP50m WC outflow and GBP14m higher interest; SBC is NOT the cause (SBC fell from 0.65% to 0.71% of revenue, flat).
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs use the owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - tax on vested awards) across the whole history: FY2020 389.5, FY2022 346.5, FY2025 292.6.

scenario_narratives.base: DEAL BREAKS, standalone base: Deal breaks, standalone base: mid-single-digit LFL growth plus bolt-ons, margin progression toward and past the 18.5%+ adjusted operating margin target, 26% cash tax, leases expensed, NCI deducted.
scenario_narratives.bull: DEAL COMPLETES (replaces the standalone bull): the EQT/Isotope Bidco scheme becomes effective around end-Jan 2027 (midpoint of the guided Q4 2026 / Q1 2027 window) and holders receive GBP60.00 cash per share - the GBP61.077 headline less the 107.7p FY2025 final dividend already paid; no interim dividend is being declared. PV at 5.0% over 0.31 years = 5909.93p.
scenario_narratives.bear: DEAL BREAKS, standalone bear: Deal breaks on a regulatory block into a consumer-sourcing/energy downturn; growth 2-3%, margin stalls at 23% pre-SBC.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Intertek is valued as a LIVE SCHEME, per the dcf-methods routing table: the bull slot is replaced by the deal-completes scenario (PV of the GBP60.00 remaining cash consideration, 5.0% over 0.31 years = 5909.93p) and the base/bear slots are the deal-breaks standalone owner-FCF component DCF from ITRK.L_Drivers.json (base 4626.12p, bear 3212.28p; 10-year, GBP WACC 8.0%, leases expensed, NCI deducted in the bridge, SBC expensed, 26% cash tax). Weights 90/7/3 (deal-completes/base/bear) give a weighted IV of 5739.13p against 5890.0p. Risk is charged once: completion risk in the weight, time value in the 5.0% rate, business risk in the standalone legs' flows at a single 8.0% WACC. The deal-completes leg carries no growth or margin drivers, so the sensitivity grid, the required-return table and the slider engine apply to the standalone BASE leg only. The standalone three-scenario weighting (15/50/35 = 4666.52p) is retained in probability_weighted.standalone_weighted_iv and corporate_action.standalone_values for use the day the scheme lapses.
what_moves_the_number: Completion probability (sensitivity: p_0.70=5398p, p_0.80=5568p, p_0.90=5739p, p_0.95=5825p, p_0.98=5876p)
Completion date (each extra quarter at 5.0% costs ~73p on the deal leg)
Standalone base value if the scheme lapses (4,626p; the stock would fall to the standalone range)
key_risks_to_valuation: Scheme lapses on a regulatory/antitrust or FDI block, or slips past the long-stop date
Consumer-goods sourcing volumes under tariffs (standalone legs)
Rising leverage (1.4x net debt/EBITDA after the FY2025 buyback) if the business stays listed
Stale-value risk: this file is wrong the moment the scheme completes (delist) or lapses (re-weight to standalone)
valuation_philosophy.stance: HOLD to completion for existing holders; no fundamental case for new money above the standalone DCF; the arb spread is thin.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 3519-5900 GBp
data_sources.financials: ITRK.L_Metrics.csv (FY2019-FY2025 + half-years) from the FY2019-FY2025 annual reports and the H1 FY2026 half-year report; component lines cited by file:line in inputs.*
data_sources.qualitative: ITRK.L_Analysis.json (2026-10-10); H1 FY2026 half-year report EQT Transaction Update and outlook
data_sources.corporate_action: H1 FY2026 half-year report: EQT Transaction Update, outlook (no interim dividend), going-concern note (conditions, financing); Analysis JSON recent_developments (6 Aug 2026 vote 98.72%)

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 AR cash flow statement: equity-settled transactions GBP24.3m (ITRK.L_Annual_FY2025.txt:11337) plus tax paid on share awards vested GBP10.1m (line 11309); the GBP1.8m 'tax paid on share buyback' (stamp duty, line 11308) is excluded because it is a buyback cost, not compensation
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows in GBP (millions); LSE quote in pence (GBp = 1/100 GBP). fx_rate 100 converts model GBP per share to quote pence. No dual listing to parity-check; the conversion is definitional, not a market rate.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-09T16:15:00Z regular close (Yahoo chart API); not an after-hours print
inputs.share_count_basis: Diluted weighted average 154.8m, H1 FY2026 note 5 (ITRK.L_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt:1623); the GBP350m buyback completed in 2025 so the period-end count matches the half-year average. Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows (charging both would double-count).
inputs.wacc_rationale: GBP-built: 10y gilt ~4.5% + 5.0% ERP x beta ~0.9 = ~9.0% cost of equity; pre-tax cost of debt 3.9% (company's weighted average rate, H1 FY2026) = ~2.9% after 26% tax; ~16% debt weight at standalone equity value -> WACC 8.0%. Same WACC in every scenario: risk is charged once, in the scenario flows and weights, never also in the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) leases as operating cost: full lease cash (FY2025 principal GBP78.4m + IFRS 16 interest GBP11.5m = GBP89.9m, 2.6% of revenue) charged inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path; lease liabilities (GBP319.3m at 2026-06-30) EXCLUDED from net_debt; D&A for cash tax is ex right-of-use depreciation and ex acquisition-intangible amortisation (FY2025 depreciation + software amortisation GBP167.0m less ~GBP78m ROU depreciation = ~GBP89m, 2.6%).
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated (100%); non-controlling interests charged ONCE in the equity bridge: FY2026 guided NCI profit share GBP20-21m (H1 FY2026 outlook) capitalised at ~15x = GBP300m deducted. NCI equity on the balance sheet is GBP44.6m (FY2025 note 20); dividends to NCI GBP16.1m/yr.
inputs.notes: THIS DRIVERS FILE IS THE STANDALONE (DEAL-BREAKS) MODEL ONLY. Intertek is subject to a shareholder-approved (98.72%, 6 Aug 2026) take-private by EQT/Isotope Bidco under a UK scheme of arrangement; SKILL.md routes a live scheme to deal-completes vs deal-breaks weighting. The engine output from this file is the deal-breaks leg; the shipped ITRK.L_DCF.json replaces the bull slot with the deal-completes scenario (PV of the GBP60.00 remaining cash consideration) and re-weights. Model for this leg: owner-FCF component DCF, 10-year horizon, GBP. EBITDA margin is PRE-SBC (statutory EBITDA GBP745.2m + GBP24.3m SBC = GBP769.5m, 22.4%) because IFRS statutory EBITDA already expenses SBC; the engine then deducts sbc_pct once. EBITDA is statutory (after ~GBP25m/yr of cash SDIs for restructuring/M&A), i.e. deal costs and integration costs are treated as recurring for a serial bolt-on acquirer. Interest income (GBP3.7m) not stripped: the company is net debt, so there is no cash pile being double-counted. reported_fcf GBP327.0m is the company's levered definition (after GBP66.1m interest paid and GBP78.4m lease principal); last_fcf = 327.0 - 34.4 = 292.6 (levered owner FCF). The component build is UNLEVERED (interest lives in WACC), so year-1 component FCF runs ~GBP45-50m above last_fcf plus ~GBP50m of 2025 working-capital outflow that is not repeated; working capital is structurally negative (-GBP45.7m at FY2025), so wc_capture is 0. Timing: fy0 = FY2025 with Y1 = FY2026 discounted a full year, against a 2026-06-30 balance sheet -> H1 FY2026 FCF (GBP101m) is effectively counted in both, which is conservative by ~GBP0.6/share; it also correctly excludes the 107.7p FY2025 final dividend already paid. Buyback: GBP367.9m in FY2025 (GBP350m programme + employee-trust purchases) funded the flat count; no buyback since the offer. Pension: UK scheme surplus GBP31.2m, Swiss deficit GBP2.5m, net immaterial, ignored. || SHIPPED DCF JSON: bull slot replaced by the deal-completes scenario (PV of GBP60.00 remaining cash at 5.0% over 0.31 yr = 5909.93p); weights 90/7/3 deal-completes/base/bear; see corporate_action and valuation_philosophy. valuation.bull, entry_price.bull, probability_weighted and scenario_narratives.bull were written by hand over the engine output; everything else (base/bear projections, sensitivity, required_return_table, workbook sheets) is engine-derived from ITRK.L_Drivers.json.

bear.narrative: Standalone bear: the scheme lapses on a regulatory block and the business meets a trade/tariff-driven slowdown in consumer-goods sourcing and a weak World of Energy; FY2027 growth 2%, margin gives back the FY2026 gain and stalls at 23% pre-SBC; terminal growth 2%, cap 16x.

base.narrative: Standalone Intertek if the scheme lapses: FY2026 at guidance (mid-single-digit LFL plus bolt-ons; H1 +5.9% reported), decelerating to 2.5% by year 10; pre-SBC EBITDA margin from 22.4% to 24.5% (adjusted operating margin ~18.1% -> ~19.4%, past the 18.5%+ medium-term target but slower than the 240bps delivered 2023-25); capex 4.2%, cash tax 26% (guided ETR 25.5-26.5%), SBC 1.0% flat.

bull.narrative: SLIDER REFERENCE ONLY. These are the engine's standalone-bull driver paths (value 5347p); the bull SLOT in valuation/probability_weighted is the deal-completes scenario (PV of GBP60.00 cash = 5909.93p), which has no growth/margin drivers and cannot be reproduced by the slider engine. Expect the dashboard engine check to report the bull slot as not engine-derived.

bull.method: PV of the GBP60.00 remaining cash consideration under the EQT/Isotope Bidco scheme, discounted 0.31 years at 5.0% (UK short rate ~4.0% + 1.0% timing-slippage premium). Completion risk is NOT in this rate; it is charged once, in the probability weight.
bull.note: Engine fields (sum_pv_fcf, terminal_value, enterprise_value ...) do not apply to a cash-consideration scenario; the engine's standalone bull (5347p) is retained under standalone_bull_reference for the record.

bull.method: GBP60.00 remaining consideration discounted 0.31 years at the 15% hurdle

entry_price.method: Deal-weighted: P x PV(offer at 15% hurdle) + base/bear weights x standalone 10-year hurdle entry prices. The standalone legs' hurdle entry prices (~1442p/1017p) are far below the deal PV because they demand 15% from an 8%-WACC business over ten years; with 90% on the deal, the weighted entry price is dominated by the offer.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 20x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Deal-completes vs deal-breaks weighting (SKILL.md live-scheme row), not three growth scenarios. bull slot = deal completes 90%: scheme approved by 98.72% at both the Court Meeting and General Meeting (6 Aug 2026), board-recommended, no competing bidder, fully committed financing (GBP4,430m interim term facilities + GBP800m RCF, Scheme Document 15 Jul 2026), sponsor EQT with Luxinva/Mubadala co-investors; remaining conditions are court sanction and regulatory/antitrust clearances in a 100+ country footprint (the break path: a merger-control or FDI block or a long-stop slip - TIC is not a sensitive sector and EQT has no overlapping TIC asset, so a block is unlikely but not zero four months after the 2.7 announcement). base 7% / bear 3% = deal breaks 10%, split 70/30 because a regulatory break leaves the business intact (base) and only a break that coincides with a consumer-sourcing/energy downturn lands in the bear. The market at 5890p against a ~4202p break value implies ~98% completion (offer discounted at the ~4% arb rate); the 90% here is deliberately below that, so the weighted IV sits ~2.6% under the price: the 1.9% gross spread (6.2% annualised) does not fully pay for a 10% break probability against a ~29% drawdown to the standalone value.

engine.name: dcf_engine
engine.bull_slot_override: deal_completes: valuation.bull / entry_price.bull / probability_weighted written by hand; assumptions.bull paths are the standalone-bull slider reference and do NOT reproduce valuation.bull.intrinsic_value

corporate_action.status: LIVE shareholder-approved recommended cash scheme - the share price is pinned to the deal, not to fundamentals; re-price or pull this ticker once the scheme completes or lapses
corporate_action.type: Recommended all-cash acquisition by UK scheme of arrangement (Rule 2.7 announcement 18 Jun 2026; Scheme Document 15 Jul 2026)
corporate_action.acquirer: Isotope Bidco Limited, indirectly owned by EQT X (EUR and USD SCSp) with indirect minority co-investors including Luxinva S.A. (ADIA) and Mubadala; debt financing via Isotope Finco interim facilities (GBP4,430m term + GBP800m RCF; Barclays, Credit Agricole CIB, Deutsche Bank, Morgan Stanley)
corporate_action.offer_note: GBP61.077 headline is inclusive of the 107.7p FY2025 final dividend, paid in the ordinary course; remaining cash consideration GBP60.00. No FY2026 interim dividend (board declined one to protect the consideration). Equity value ~GBP9.3bn on 154.8m diluted shares.
corporate_action.shareholder_approval: 2026-08-06: 98.72% at both the Court Meeting and the General Meeting
corporate_action.remaining_conditions: Court sanction of the scheme; regulatory/antitrust and FDI clearances (H1 FY2026 going-concern note 1)
corporate_action.timetable: Completion guided to Q4 2026 or Q1 2027; modelled at 2027-01-31 (window midpoint)
corporate_action.offer_discount_rate_basis: UK short rate ~4.0% (SONIA / 3m gilt) + 1.0% premium for timing slippage conditional on completion. EZJ.L (2026-10-10) used the 11.7% cost of equity for its deal leg; at the 9.0% CoE the ITRK leg would be 5841.83p (-68.1p, immaterial to the conclusion). Break risk is in the probability, not the rate.
corporate_action.probability_rationale: Deal-completes vs deal-breaks weighting (SKILL.md live-scheme row), not three growth scenarios. bull slot = deal completes 90%: scheme approved by 98.72% at both the Court Meeting and General Meeting (6 Aug 2026), board-recommended, no competing bidder, fully committed financing (GBP4,430m interim term facilities + GBP800m RCF, Scheme Document 15 Jul 2026), sponsor EQT with Luxinva/Mubadala co-investors; remaining conditions are court sanction and regulatory/antitrust clearances in a 100+ country footprint (the break path: a merger-control or FDI block or a long-stop slip - TIC is not a sensitive sector and EQT has no overlapping TIC asset, so a block is unlikely but not zero four months after the 2.7 announcement). base 7% / bear 3% = deal breaks 10%, split 70/30 because a regulatory break leaves the business intact (base) and only a break that coincides with a consumer-sourcing/energy downturn lands in the bear. The market at 5890p against a ~4202p break value implies ~98% completion (offer discounted at the ~4% arb rate); the 90% here is deliberately below that, so the weighted IV sits ~2.6% under the price: the 1.9% gross spread (6.2% annualised) does not fully pay for a 10% break probability against a ~29% drawdown to the standalone value.
corporate_action.deal_breaks_value_basis: 0.70 x standalone base (4626.12p) + 0.30 x standalone bear (3212.28p) from the owner-FCF component engine (ITRK.L_Drivers.json); the engine's own 15/50/35 standalone weighting is 4666.52p
corporate_action.undisturbed_price_reference: 52-week low 3519p; the stock traded ~4,200-4,800p in H1 2026 before the approach, i.e. around the standalone DCF, so a break would most likely reset the shares toward ~4,200-4,600p (-22% to -29%)
corporate_action.market_implied_probability_note: At 5890.0p against a 4201.97p break value with the offer discounted at ~4% over 0.31 years, the market implies ~98% completion. Gross spread 1.87%, ~6.2% annualised.
corporate_action.deal_weighted_iv_formula: P x PV(offer) + 0.07 x base + 0.03 x bear = 0.9 x 5909.93 + 0.07 x 4626.12 + 0.03 x 3212.28 = probability_weighted.weighted_iv
corporate_action.reading: The actionable value is probability_weighted.weighted_iv (5739.13p), which IS the deal-weighted number in this file (unlike EZJ.L, where the deal lives only in corporate_action). At 5890.0p a holder earns ~1.9% (~6.2% annualised) if the scheme completes by end-Jan 2027 and faces ~-29% if it lapses; that is adequate only above ~96% completion probability. Existing holders: hold to completion (the 60.00 cash is worth more than the standalone business on every leg); new money: not a fundamental buy - the standalone DCF is 4,626p base - only an arb position, and a thin one.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.manual_recompute_note: sanity_check.py's printed multiples are off by the known GBP/GBp fx_rate direction bug (implied x100, historical x10,000: FY2025 'price' 462,600 is 4,626p x 100). Hand recompute at the deal-weighted IV 5739p = GBP57.39 on FY2025 statutory figures: P/E 26.6x (EPS GBP2.16), P/B 8.4x (equity GBP1,082.9m / 159.0m basic shares = GBP6.81), EV/EBITDA 13.9x (equity GBP8,884m on 154.8m diluted + net debt GBP1,145.5m at 2026-06-30 + NCI ~GBP300m = EV ~GBP10,330m / EBITDA GBP745.2m), P/S 2.6x. The stock traded 4,034-5,852p over FY2019-FY2025 (P/E ~20-30x), and the EQT offer itself is ~14x FY2025 EBITDA / ~28x statutory EPS, so the valuation sits inside the company's own range; the 'passed' verdict is correct but by coincidence of the bug, not by the script's arithmetic. The script's trip rules are built for a going-concern owner-FCF DCF; for a deal-weighted value the relevant check is the one in corporate_action (break value vs offer vs market-implied probability), not multiples. Not looped: the bug is systemic (see memory) and needs a TDD fix plus corpus recompute, not a per-ticker patch.
